label: H.R. 4077

latest_action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 4077, titled the GUARD Veterans' Health Care Act, allows the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to recover costs from Medicare Advantage and Medicare prescription drug plans when the VA provides health care items or services to individuals enrolled in those plans. It also updates and expands the authority of the United States to recover reasonable charges for care or services furnished to veterans for non-service-connected disabilities from various third parties, including tort liability cases and other insurance types. Additionally, the bill sets strict timelines, payment requirements, interest rates for late payments, and civil penalties for third parties failing to comply with reimbursement demands.

affected_groups.effect: Gains explicit authority to collect reimbursements from Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans and strengthens mechanisms to recover costs from third parties, depositing funds into the VA Medical Care Collections Fund.

Required to reimburse the VA for health care items and services covered under their plans that are provided to dual-enrolled individuals, subject to strict timelines, interest rules, and potential penalties.
affected_groups.group: Medicare Advantage and Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Sponsors

affected_groups.effect: Subject to stricter rules, 45-day payment timelines, mandatory information-sharing regarding beneficiary benefits, and heavy civil penalties or damages for failing to reimburse the United States for non-service-connected care.
Receives care through the VA while allowing the government to coordinate benefits and recover costs from their other health plans or third-party settlements.
affected_groups.group: Veterans Enrolled in Medicare Advantage or Receiving Non-Service-Connected Care

key_provisions: Permits the VA to recover costs from Medicare Advantage plans and Medicare prescription drug plans for covered health care items and services provided to enrolled individuals, starting with plan years on or after January 1, 2026.

Requires Medicare Advantage organizations and prescription drug plan sponsors to reimburse the VA regardless of any additional administrative requirements or utilization management imposed by the plan.

Expands the federal government's authority to recover or collect reasonable charges for non-service-connected care from third parties, including situations involving tort liability, negligence, and non-health-plan coverages like underinsured motorist coverage.

Establishes a 45-day deadline for third parties to pay a clean claim, provide written notice of refusal with reasons, or request additional information after receiving a claim or settlement resolution.
Requires third parties to pay monthly interest on unpaid claims after the 45-day window and limits third-party requests for payment error refunds to 18 months.

Enforces civil penalties and potential damages (including triple the claim amount or up to $50,000 for willful failures, and double damages for certain failures) on third parties that fail to comply with reimbursement requirements.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 4077, titled the GUARD Veterans' Health Care Act, allows the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to recover costs from Medicare Advantage and Medicare prescription drug plans when the VA provides health care items or services to individuals enrolled in those plans. It also updates and expands the authority of the United States to recover reasonable charges for care or services furnished to veterans for non-service-connected disabilities from various third parties, including tort liability cases and other insurance types. Additionally, the bill sets strict timelines, payment requirements, interest rates for late payments, and civil penalties for third parties failing to comply with reimbursement demands.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation alters the intersection of veterans' healthcare and private Medicare or third-party insurance payments by creating a direct pipeline for the VA to recoup expenses from Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans. By imposing rigid timelines, interest, and severe financial penalties on third parties, the bill attempts to maximize federal cost recovery for care delivered to veterans.
